questions.q: What will Yahweh do to Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh will again choose Israel and restore them into their own land.

questions.q: Will anyone else go with the Israelites back to their land?
questions.a: Foreigners will join with them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.

questions.q: Who will bring the Israelites back to their own land?
questions.a: The nations will bring them to their own place.

questions.q: What will the house of Israel do to those nations that took Israel captive?
questions.a: The house of Israel will take them as male and female servants. They will take captive those who had captured them and they will rule over their oppressors.

questions.q: What will happen on the day that Yahweh gives Israel rest from their suffering, anguish, and hard labor?
questions.a: They will sing a song taunting the king of Babylon.

questions.q: What has happened to the oppressor?
questions.a: The oppressor has come to an end.

questions.q: What has Yahweh taken away from the wicked ruler?
questions.a: Yahweh has taken away the power of the wicked ruler.

questions.q: What had the king of Babylon done?
questions.a: He had struck the people in wrath with unceasing blows. He had ruled the nations in anger, with an attack that was unrestrained.

questions.q: What are people throughout the earth doing now?
questions.a: People throughout the earth are resting peacefully and singing happy songs.

questions.q: What do the cedars of Lebanon say now that the king of Babylon is gone?
questions.a: The cedars of Lebanon say that no one comes to cut them down anymore.

questions.q: What happens in Sheol when the king of Babylon arrives?
questions.a: Sheol trembles to meet him, and it wakes up the spirits of dead leaders and kings to greet him.

questions.q: What will the dead kings of the earth say to the king of Babylon?
questions.a: They will say, “You have become as weak as us…” and “Your pride has been brought down to Sheol….”

questions.q: What has happened to the king of Babylon?
questions.a: He has fallen from the heavens and been cut down to the ground.

questions.q: What did the king of Babylon say in his heart?
questions.a: He said he would exalt his throne above the stars of God and make himself like the Most High.

questions.q: To where has the king of Babylon been brought down?
questions.a: He has been brought down to Sheol, to the deepest part of the Pit.

questions.q: What will those who see the king of Babylon in Sheol say about him?
questions.a: They will ask if this is the man who made the earth tremble, shook kingdoms, turned the world into a wilderness, and would not let his prisoners go home.

questions.q: How are other kings of the nations usually buried?
questions.a: Other kings are usually buried honorably, each in a tomb of his own.

questions.q: What has happened to the king of Babylon’s body instead of being buried?
questions.a: His body has been thrown away like a useless branch, among the bodies of soldiers killed in battle, like a trampled corpse.

questions.q: Why will the king of Babylon not join the other kings of the nations in burial?
questions.a: He will not join them because he destroyed his land and killed his people.

questions.q: What is commanded should happen to the king of Babylon’s sons?
questions.a: They should be killed, so that they cannot rise up, take over the earth, and fill the world with their cities.

questions.q: What is the declaration of Yahweh of Armies against Babylon?
questions.a: He declares, “I will arise against them” and further, “I will cut off from Babylon name, remnant, offspring, and posterity.”

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to Babylon?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will turn Babylon into a swampy marshland and sweep it away with the broom of destruction.

questions.q: What has Yahweh of Armies sworn?
questions.a: Yahweh has sworn that what he has planned will certainly happen, just as he has determined.

questions.q: What has Yahweh of Armies sworn concerning the Assyrian in Yahweh’s land?
questions.a: He said he would break the Assyrian in his land and on his mountains trample him under foot.

questions.q: What is Yahweh’s plan for?
questions.a: Yahweh’s plan is for the whole earth, and his power is stretched out over all the nations.

questions.q: Who can stop what Yahweh of Armies has determined to do?
questions.a: No one can stop him or turn back his hand.

questions.q: When did Yahweh give this message?
questions.a: Yahweh gave this message during the year that King Ahaz died.

questions.q: What was the declaration against Philistia?
questions.a: It was declared that Philistia should not rejoice, for Yahweh was going to kill Philistia’s root with famine that will put to death all Philistia’s survivors.

questions.q: What is coming from the north against Philistia?
questions.a: A great army is coming from the north, like a thick cloud of smoke, and none of its soldiers fall behind.

questions.q: Who founded Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh founded Zion.

questions.q: What will the poor of Yahweh’s people find in Zion?
questions.a: The poor of Yahweh’s people will find refuge in Zion.

commentary.text: The destruction of Babylon, and the death of its proud monarch. (Is. 14:1-23) Assurance of the destruction of Assyria. (Is. 14:24-27) The destruction of the Philistines. (Is. 14:28-32)

Is. 14:1-23 The whole plan of Divine Providence is arranged with a view to the good of the people of God. A settlement in the land of promise is of God's mercy. Let the church receive those whom God receives. God's people, wherever their lot is cast, should endeavour to recommend religion by a right and winning conversation. Those that would not be reconciled to them, should be humbled by them. This may be applied to the success of the gospel, when those were brought to obey it who had opposed it. God himself undertakes to work a blessed change. They shall have rest from their sorrow and fear, the sense of their present burdens, and the dread of worse. Babylon abounded in riches. The king of Babylon having the absolute command of so much wealth, by the help of it ruled the nations. This refers especially to the people of the Jews; and it filled up the measure of the king of Babylon's sins. Tyrants sacrifice their true interest to their lusts and passions. It is gracious ambition to covet to be like the Most Holy, for he has said, Be ye holy, for I am holy; but it is sinful ambition to aim to be like the Most High, for he has said, He who exalts himself shall be abased. The devil thus drew our first parents to sin. Utter ruin should be brought upon him. Those that will not cease to sin, God will make to cease. He should be slain, and go down to the grave; this is the common fate of tyrants. True glory, that is, true grace, will go up with the soul to heaven, but vain pomp will go down with the body to the grave; there is an end of it. To be denied burial, if for righteousness' sake, may be rejoiced in, Matt. 5:12. But if the just punishment of sin, it denotes that impenitent sinners shall rise to everlasting shame and contempt. Many triumphs should be in his fall. God will reckon with those that disturb the peace of mankind. The receiving the king of Babylon into the regions of the dead, shows there is a world of spirits, to which the souls of men remove at death. And that souls have converse with each other, though we have none with them; and that death and hell will be death and hell indeed, to all who fall unholy, from the height of this world's pomps, and the fulness of its pleasures. Learn from all this, that the seed of evil-doers shall never be renowned. The royal city is to be ruined and forsaken. Thus the utter destruction of the New Testament Babylon is illustrated, Rev. 18:2. When a people will not be made clean with the besom of reformation, what can they expect but to be swept off the face of the earth with the besom of destruction?

Is. 14:24-27 Let those that make themselves a yoke and a burden to God's people, see what they are to expect. Let those that are the called according to God's purpose, comfort themselves, that whatever God has purposed, it shall stand. The Lord of hosts has purposed to break the Assyrian's yoke; his hand is stretched out to execute this purpose; who has power to turn it back? By such dispensations of providence, the Almighty shows in the most convincing manner, that sin is hateful in his sight.

Is. 14:28-32 Assurance is given of the destruction of the Philistines and their power, by famine and war. Hezekiah would be more terrible to them than Uzziah had been. Instead of rejoicing, there would be lamentation, for the whole land would be ruined. Such destruction will come upon the proud and rebellious, but the Lord founded Zion for a refuge to poor sinners, who flee from the wrath to come, and trust in his mercy through Christ Jesus. Let us tell all around of our comforts and security, and exhort them to seek the same refuge and salvation.
